keyFindings.description: The usage() text a developer reads from `e2e-local.sh --help` still says 'NATS runs in Docker, or as a local nats-server process on a host that has no container runtime.' Neither is true at this head: the script builds and starts internal/testnats/cmd/natsd, which the file's own header comment at :5-6 says correctly, so the one file contradicts itself twenty lines apart and the only thing --help says about where NATS comes from is wrong in both halves. Introduced by this round, which deleted the mechanism and left the sentence. Both thermonuclear passes found it independently. Two lines.

The comment above this rig's deferral set makes two claims the code does not support. 'One deferral set per handler, as main.go builds it' is the inverse of what main.go does: main.go:799 builds one set for the process and shares it through deliveryConfig with every handler, which is the invariant that took three rounds to establish and whose absence was the round-two blocking finding. And 'an agent delivery this rig cannot place is held here and retried rather than acknowledged away' is false of this rig: it never sets unplaceableRetryWindow, so the window is zero and delivery.go gives such a message up on its first delivery. Added by the previous round's merge; the previous round's security pass half-flagged it and the reviewer let it through as an observation, which was the reviewer's error to correct here. Two lines.

keyFindings.description: The disposition line reads 'no production change - the cancellation window does not exist, ensureConnWithContext's reconnect wait selects on ctx.Done()'. The window does exist and is narrowed rather than closed: ensureConnWithContext returns at the top of its loop on IsConnected||IsDraining without consulting ctx, its ctx.Done() arm sits only in the select taken when the connection is down but not closed and beside a 10 ms timer Go may pick, and a successful connectWithContext returns nil whatever the context did. The same body's Not proven / risk entry says so and says it supersedes implement.json's identical claim - so the body now contradicts itself, and the merger quotes this body into the READY packet, which lands on the Dispatch issue permanently. One clause.
